chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Haysam ibn Abi Masrouq, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Hilal ibn Khaqan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who neglects Zakat, while it has been obligated for him, is like the one who withholds it, while it has been obligated upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between neglecting Zakat and withholding it according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the legal status of one who neglects obligatory Zakat is identical to that of one who actively withholds it, emphasizing that mere omission carries the same weight as deliberate refusal. This ruling underscores the seriousness of Zakat as a mandatory pillar rather than a voluntary charity, a view supported by Shia jurists who argue that the obligation is fulfilled by the act of payment regardless of the payer's internal intent. The hadith serves as a critical legal precedent in Usul al-Fiqh for equating the sin and liability of negligence with that of explicit denial in financial obligations.
